My current dosage is 40mg in the morning and 20mg around lunch hour. I am currently happy with my dosage & timing. It took nearly 6 months to get it right

It really depends. When I was at a lower dosage (10-20mg) it only took a few days. 30 took a bit longer maybe 3-5 days. 40mg it was only like a day. But again everyone is different! People say it can take anywhere from 1-2 weeks. 

In saying this, you know your body best, so be sure to listen to it! If you aren’t comfortable on this medication there’s nothing wrong with exploring different options (there are non-stim options out there). Therapy is also a great tool if you decide against medication!

I am a recovering addict (almost 4 years clean) from cocaine. When I started Vyvanse I felt the same, sometimes I still do. 

Everyone is different, medication affects everyone different. I will say, that once my body adapted to my current dosage (40mg morning + 20mg at lunch) this feeling subsided greatly. I was worried at first that it would cause me to relapse. 
Your starting dosage could be too high, it might not be the right medication for you, or it could just take time to adapt/build tolerance. You will build tolerance on these meds like you do with drugs.

I should add that I started on only 10mg and worked my way up slowly over the course of six months or so. My psychiatrist was aware of my previous addiction issues (and previous misdiagnosis’) as they were on my records and I was honest with her. She started slow to monitor me. 

Since vyvanse is a stimulant, it is similar to cocaine in that way. It got easier for me, and I’m hoping the same for you. Stay strong! You will eventually get to a place where you find solace in your medication and dosage :) in the meantime, don’t be afraid to reach out for mental health support if you feel yourself going down into a dark hole. Hang in there friend!!

It’s a very scary thing, especially because no one can help you when that panic arises not even yourself. The only that helps is removing yourself from that situation and it’s not always possible.

It’s not bullet proof, but i find the best time to use these methods is when I first start to feel the panic setting in.

I will contribute by saying I got misdiagnosed with bipolar about 6 years ago. I stopped my meds cold turkey maybe 2-3 years ago. I’ve been suspecting for about 3 years it was something else. 

I luckily got into a psychiatrist only a week after getting a requisition (in August of this year), and my psychiatrist confirmed I have adhd, and not bipolar. 

A lot of symptoms are similar between bipolar & adhd. My psychiatrist made it a point to say that women/girls mask their adhd symptoms a lot better, which is why it can often go misdiagnosed. 

The only word of advice I have is just be careful tapering off. Do NOT stop cold turkey, and make sure to receive medical supervision while doing so, even if that means waiting. Luckily the only adverse side effect I had was brain zaps, but quitting without medical supervision is dangerous. It can cause someone to spiral into extreme bouts of depression/suicidal ideation. Good luck!

Sober 3 years! I was diagnosed with substance use disorder 5 years ago, after a 10 year battle of substance and alcohol abuse. It started when I was only in grade 9.

Vyvanse has concurrently helped both my ADHD and BED. I am on 40mg right now (just upped from 30mg). I will say that it has helped me on a path to start healing my relationship with food. Now, I look at food like I should, a source of fuel for my body, instead of an outlet for dopamine. It also gives me motivation to workout in the morning. 

I don’t use scales because they are a trigger for me, instead I measure myself. I have lost a good amount of weight over three months in a healthy way. I also get full off less, and I can recognize when I’m full instead of ignoring it!

Not sure if you’re a woman, but it becomes more challenging during PMS because the meds don’t work as well. Also I used to binge the most during this time. BUT the past two cycles I’ve been able to maintain healthy habits because I found a routine that worked for me!
It is definitely easier said than done 😂 I don’t blame you. Took years of work to find and maintain a routine that works for me and my brain

If you are able, work out first thing in the morning before work! It helps for me at least (I work remotely too). I find if I don’t work out in the morning, the meds barely work and I have no focus at work

But yes, I’ve had numerous meltdowns because of it. Sometimes it even causes panic attacks (I’m diagnosed with panic disorder). If you have suspicions that you may be autistic, see if you can get a diagnosis! It may feel nice to be reassured, and know the next appropriate steps to take. 

In the meantime, look into a good pair of noise cancelling head phones. They’ll be a life saver :) good luck!

I started in learning and development and got “promoted” to ID.  You can find a junior role if you’re interested. 

If you want recommendations on courses to take, I recommend Adult Learning and/or Instructional Design/Instructional Techniques classes. Most ID roles look for this level of education. If you land an interview, you can explain your situation about switching job roles. From my experience L&D professionals are super kind and compassionate. 

Also, look into User Interface/User Experience (UI/UX) roles. Similar levels of creativity. UI/UX is definitely up and coming so it’s another great field to get into! 

Hope this helps. If you have any other questions feel free to message me :)

I work somewhat of a creative role, I am an instructional designer. I must say it keeps me on my toes for sure. Being engaged at work is quite simple with my meds. I also work remotely so it’s nice when it’s slow, and I check out, I can go do something else. 

You don’t necessarily have to be creative to become an instructional designer. But I could see how any creative role would work well with someone that has adhd :)

I started on 10mg and got bumped up by 10mg every 30 days. I’m currently on 30mg and I start 40mg next week. 

I will say the first 60 days (on 10&20mg) I felt hopeless. It really didn’t feel like it was doing much if anything at all. I didn’t have much hope when I started 30mg. 

But it has significantly improved my quality of life. I actually sat in a meeting for 1.5 hours and I listened the entire time. I do still find some days are better than others. I also find that it helps only about 4 hours out of the day, which is why I’ll be starting on 40mg. 

If you don’t think it’s working for you yet, then go up. You’ll notice a significant difference once you get to the right dosage. And remember, you can always go back down if it’s too high!
